member.name: T:BlocksOs.Api.Controllers.AdyenWebhookController
member.summary: Where Adyen tells us what actually happened.
member.remarks:
Deliberately anonymous. Adyen calls it with no token of ours, so this endpoint cannot sit behind [ProtectedEndPoint] or [ProjectPolicy] like everything else in this service. Adding either would not secure it — it would simply stop payments being confirmed.
What secures it instead is the HMAC signature on every item, checked against the key in the vault. An unsigned or wrongly signed item is discarded without being acted on. It should also be unreachable from outside the cluster; the signature is the last line, not the only one.
Adyen retries until it receives [accepted], so the response says that whatever we made of the batch — refusing would only make it resend something we will never accept — and every item is claimed by its pspReference so a redelivery changes nothing.

member.summary: Stores a public certificate for the calling tenant and returns the URL to read it back.
member.remarks:
The file arrives as multipart form data while the flag arrives on the query string, so both are bound explicitly - a single complex parameter would be inferred as [FromBody] and reject the upload. Callers also send a TenantId query parameter; it is ignored, because the tenant comes from the request context.
Gated by the same permission as UpdateTokenValidationParameters, which persists the URL this returns. The certificate is what token validation actually trusts, so it must not be writable by someone who cannot edit the configuration pointing at it.

member.name: T:BlocksOs.Api.Controllers.CheckoutController
member.summary: Buying environments and top-ups for a project.
member.remarks:
Two calls, in this order and no other.
start prices and validates the purchase, writes it as a pending order, and returns the idempotency key. Everything knowable is checked here, while refusing still costs nothing.
pay charges the card and hands provisioning to the worker. It returns as soon as the money clears — building seven environments takes minutes, and no HTTP call waits for that.
Both are owner-only. Money is the case exists for: it is a flag rather than a grant string so that nothing typed into a hand-edited policy list can satisfy it.

member.summary: What a project is using, and the sync that gives an environment rows for anything new in the catalogue.
member.remarks:
Scoped by project group, never by the caller's own tenant. A tenant is one environment and a project is a group of them, so the subject of every call here is the group — which is also what authorises against, so the read and the access check agree on one identifier.
The rows live in the platform's root database. Nothing on this controller can reach a tenant database, and nothing infers a tenant from the caller: a request that does not name a group is refused rather than quietly answered for whichever project the caller happened to have open.

member.summary: IAM's OIDC callback sets an httpOnly access-token cookie named after the redirect host (e.g. dev-os-612.blocksdevelopers.com on PR previews, dev-os.blocksdevelopers.com on the shared dev host).
